segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsections 3 and 4,
shall not drive on the left side of the highway within such zone or drive across or on the left side of any pavement striping designed to mark such zone throughout its length.
A driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such zone
to an adjoining highway if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
and there will be no impediment to
a driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such a zone
if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
and if it would not be an impediment to

elements.justification: DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'driver' means 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'. The driver is a relational role, not membership (ru.aggregate: 'Not a stand-in for: a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle'), so the role is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle (observable_reading agency) and the binder is the vehicle, 'true when the user carries an included class' of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the same mapping the index records for 'a driver'.

(i) The left side of the highway is the side to the left of the line dividing its two directions: st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the highway the subject occupies by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'; we read the way, not the roadway, so its exclusion does not apply). Being on the left side is read with prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', against half the body's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'): the body is on the left side where the line's offset is below half the width by more than p.lateral_position_tolerance. (ii) 'Such zone' is the no-passing zone the section's first subsection lets an authority indicate 'by appropriate signs or markings'. A sign: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind in {..., no_passing, ...}; end attribute', with dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', on a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the sign read is a beginning sign (end false); its 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' does not apply since no legend condition is read. A marking: st.lane_marking, 'per side of a lane: type in {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour in {white, yellow, other}', on the left side of the st.lane the subject occupies: a solid or double_solid yellow line marks the zone for that lane; a solid_broken line, whose solid half the atom does not place, leaves membership unknown. The zone's presence on the road is the evidence of its designation (status). (iii) The pavement striping designed to mark the zone is that no-passing marking (st.lane_marking type solid or double_solid, colour yellow, on the left side of the subject's lane), which on a two-way highway lies along st.centre_line. Driving across it or on its left side is the body reaching past that line: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line ('left positive') below half the width from kin.extent less p.lateral_position_tolerance. 'Throughout its length' is read by judging every observation at which the subject is in the zone.

The permitted act is the same crossing the obligation forbids: the vehicle's body reaching past the zone's centre-line striping, prim.region_lateral_offset ('left positive') against half the kin.extent width; 'A driver' is the vehicle, as in s2.

'To an adjoining highway' states where the crossing leads, a purpose read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') other than the highway h of the zone and no longer occupies h. 'Has first given the appropriate turn signal': sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}', showing left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {..., left, ...}', meaning left, at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since). The indicator's 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' does not apply: the signal is read, not the manoeuvre.

The same crossing as s6 (prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line against half the kin.extent width) by the vehicle. The region at which the left-hand turn of s11 is declared is the place a left turn leaves the highway for: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'); the declared intention takes one of them as its target.

'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'. Oncoming: rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos; its exclusion (not the direction a road user approaches an intersection from) does not apply, as the words concern road users meeting the subject head-on on this highway. Following: a member behind the subject, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for ... immediately to the rear)' (rel.bearing, negative longitudinal component), with 'headings aligned' (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.contest_same_direction_cos).

As s8b: members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that are oncoming (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing') or following (behind by rel.bearing, 'immediately to the rear', with rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

The appropriate signal for a crossing to the left to make a left-hand turn is sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'), given at the last observation before the crossing began; its manner and distance are the compliance with NRS 484B.413 composed on s13. Not the turn itself (indicator's exclusion).

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a road user of traffic is impeded where its centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; oncoming is rel.oncoming within the opposed-heading tolerance, following is a road user behind the subject (negative longitudinal bearing) with headings aligned within the same-direction tolerance; read at every observation of the crossing

traffic-conflict technique: the crossing is safe where no road user of the scene is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; read at every observation of the crossing

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: as for s8: traffic-conflict technique on oncoming (rel.oncoming) and following (behind, headings aligned) members of traffic, read at every observation of the crossing

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

residues.why: 'Except where otherwise provided' defers to provisions it does not name; those provisions are judged by their own rules, and this rule's verdict on crossing the striping to make a left-hand turn is the same whether or not they apply.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a highway h on which a centre line c lies, and is within a no-passing zone: it occupies a travel region that a dev.zone_sign of kind no_passing (end false) governs, or it occupies a lane whose left-side st.lane_marking is solid or double_solid and yellow (where that marking is solid_broken, membership is unknown).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's body does not reach past the centre line c to its left: the lateral offset of c from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, left positive) is not below half the subject's width (kin.extent) minus p.lateral_position_tolerance. A crossing is excused (E3) where, within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead, the subject occupies a highway other than h and no longer occupies h; at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since) its turn indicator showed left or its hand signal meant left; and at every observation of the crossing no member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is oncoming (rel.oncoming, p.oncoming_heading_cos) or following (behind by rel.bearing, rel.same_direction within p.contest_same_direction_cos) has a closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A crossing is also excused (E4) where the subject's declared intention int.left_turn at an intersection or a driveway/alley entrance holds at the observation; the left signal was given as in E3; NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with for the subject; no road user is in contact with the subject or has such a closest approach (safe); and no oncoming or following member of traffic has such a closest approach (impediment).

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

The striping designed to mark the zone is read where it lies along the centre line dividing the two directions; a no-passing marking between two lanes of the same direction is not read as the zone's striping.
'to an adjoining highway' is read through the conduct it explains: the subject reaching another highway within the turn window after the crossing
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic; a slowing of traffic without such a conflict is not read
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies a lane whose left st.lane_marking is solid yellow; it moves left until prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line is -1.0 m to overtake a slower vehicle; int.left_turn is declared false at every region and it stays on the same highway.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the same no-passing lane (left marking solid yellow) and keeps the centre line 0.9 m to its left with a body width of 1.8 m plus margin: the offset stays above half its width minus the tolerance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject's lane has a broken white left marking and no no_passing dev.zone_sign governs any region it occupies; it crosses the centre line to overtake.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe st.lane_marking and no zone sign is in the scene; the subject's body reaches past the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: In the no-passing zone the subject's int.left_turn is declared true at a driveway_or_alley_entrance; its left indicator has been on for the last 120 m and NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with; it crosses the centre line; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but sig.turn_indicator is off and sig.hand_signal no_signal at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but an oncoming vehicle (rel.oncoming) has a closest approach to the subject in 2 s at a centre distance of 1 m.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but the left indicator came on only 10 m before the crossing, so NRS_484B_413_2 is violated although a signal was given at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: In the zone the subject signals left, crosses the centre line and within the turn window occupies another highway and no longer the zone's highway; no oncoming or following road user has a conflicting closest approach.

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
param_proposals.source: naturalistic lane-keeping studies; source position error

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance (left-turn time gap 7.5 s) plus a margin

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions

param_proposals.name: p.contest_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 18 degrees) for travel in the same direction
